name: epoch-exhausted
why: the recorded epoch's allowance is spent; the control for the rewind below

name: epoch-rewind
why: THE EXPLOIT. claimedDaa is agent-supplied and bounded below only, so an earlier epoch used to reset spentThisEpoch to zero and hand back the whole allowance, repeatably. The per-epoch cap limited nothing.

name: epoch-forward
why: a LATER epoch legitimately carries a fresh allowance; the ratchet must not block it

name: epoch-same-headroom
why: the recorded epoch with room left is an ordinary spend

name: past-expiry
why: a claimedDaa at or beyond expiresAt. The spend path had no expiry check at all.

name: reabsorb-honest
why: an ordinary settlement: the parent takes back the child at the top of its reserve stack, releasing the child's budget and inheriting what the child actually spent. The control for the three below.

name: settle-steal
why: THE SUSPECTED HOLE. `settle` requires the revocation key and checks that output 0 receives inputs[0].value + inputs[1].value - maxFee, but it never constrains output 0's scriptPubKey and nothing ties the second input to a parent. So the revocation key alone, plus any dust it already owns, sweeps a child's whole balance to an address of its choosing. If accepted, the revocation key is a TAKE capability over children, not a STOP one.

name: reabsorb-live-grandchild
why: the child still has 1 KAS reserved for a grandchild of its own. Settling it releases the parent's reserve IN FULL while that coin sits in a grandchild that nothing can ever reabsorb, because the only grant that could — its parent — has just been consumed.

name: reabsorb-out-of-order
why: reserveRoot is a hash chain, so only the most recently delegated child can be popped. This settles the FIRST of two children while the second is still outstanding, by claiming a prevRoot that does not rebuild the parent's root.

name: revoke-honest
why: an ordinary revoke, paying the principal and a normal fee

name: revoke-burn
why: 1 sompi to the principal, the rest burned as fee. The exit paths checked the output's scriptPubKey and never its value, which made the revocation key a DESTROY capability rather than a STOP one.
